roleQuestion.instructions: Which Tower Defense role best describes the unit's main contribution in the selected upgrade configuration? Choose exactly one. Prefer the role that explains why the unit is deployed, not its weapon appearance or original game class.

criteria.basic_dps: Deals reliable direct damage without a stronger specialization in the other roles.
criteria.sniper: Prioritizes long-range, accurate, high-impact attacks against selected targets.
criteria.rapid_fire: Deals sustained damage through very frequent attacks or dense projectile volleys.
criteria.splash: Clears groups through explosions, area attacks, bouncing attacks, or chain damage.
criteria.slow: Primarily reduces movement speed or repeatedly pushes enemies backward.
criteria.support: Primarily improves other units through buffs, detection, discounts, or cooldown reduction.
criteria.economy: Primarily generates money, resources, or recoverable economic value.
criteria.tank_killer: Specializes in high-health enemies, armored enemies, bosses, or large single-target bursts.
criteria.status: Primarily applies hard control or harmful effects such as stun, freeze, burn, poison, or damage vulnerability.
criteria.summoner: Primarily deploys autonomous attackers, minions, or persistent traps that deal damage or control enemies.

classificationRules: Choose a role for the selected build, not permanently for every upgrade of a tower.
towerdefense_type on a tower is an editorial family default. base_towerdefense_type describes the unupgraded unit. Mature path roles are separate.
Use secondary_roles for hybrids. When one choice is required, select the main reason the unit is deployed.
Use slow for movement-speed reduction and repeated knockback. Use status for hard control, damaging status effects and vulnerability; use support when the main value is improving other towers.
A tower does not become tank_killer merely because it can damage a boss. The build must specialize in high-health targets.

progression.crosspath_note: Ordinary builds use one main path and at most two tiers of one other path. Crosspath prices can be added from incremental prices, but crosspath combat behavior is not simply additive. Special game modes may change these rules.

limitations: Sources are not pinned to a single game patch or repository commit. Access dates do not prove patch currency, and cached source revisions can differ.
All 26 tower names and all 390 regular upgrade names, incremental Medium source prices and short factual effects are covered; Monkeyopolis is conditional rather than a fixed price.

The export is not literally every game value. Complete crosspath stats, projectile behaviors, cooldowns, durations, degree scaling, targeting exceptions, damage modifiers, unlock conditions, patch histories, assets and lore were not fully extracted.
Easy, Hard and Impoppable prices are calculations using the cited community price function. They are not independently confirmed in-game values.
The general cost table and exported models are separate snapshots and can disagree. Older wiki base costs and XP are stored separately rather than silently merged.
The Paragon section is an inventory of 13 records found in the export, not a claim that all 13 are currently released.
Null means not verified, not applicable, or conditional as explained by the surrounding field. Null does not mean zero.
Descriptions are original factual summaries. No full wiki articles, artwork or game assets are reproduced.

records.qualification: Direct add is supported. Requires the supplied base attack and chosen game scale.
Interval change supported; the summary does not provide a factor.

records.sourceDescription: Adds more range and Camo detection.
records.qualification: Detection is personal. Range amount is missing.
Three projectiles can be declared, but current DSL aims every projectile at one primary target. A spread is a new operation.

records.sourceDescription: Changes the weapon to a long-range crossbow with three damage per hit.
records.qualification: Damage 3 is explicit; full range is not. These are source values, not balanced adaptation values.
Supported paired slow magnitude/duration requires values.

records.sourceDescription: Adds damage over time to glued targets.
records.qualification: Current periodic damage vocabulary is burn with a fixed refresh rule. Acid can only be an explicitly approved adaptation, not an asserted exact match.

records.sourceDescription: Replaces darts with slower, high-pierce balls that rebound from walls.
records.qualification: Rebound trajectory and collision are unsupported.

records.sourceDescription: Adds faster attacks and periodic critical hits.
records.qualification: Interval is tunable; periodic critical triggers and separate damage are unsupported.

records.sourceDescription: Temporarily transforms up to ten nearby Dart Monkeys; also improves regular attack speed.
records.qualification: Current manual boost affects self only; allied targeting and transformation are unsupported.

records.sourceDescription: Allows glue to slow eligible MOAB-class targets.
records.qualification: Definition can globally change existing immunity arrays, but a purchased per-attack target exception is not represented.

records.sourceDescription: Applies the global glue effect repeatedly for twenty seconds.
records.qualification: Global delivery, repeated ability effects and damage vulnerability are outside self-boost support.

records.sourceDescription: Improves cash drops, adds Elite targeting, and buffs other Snipers' attack speed.
records.qualification: Economy, custom targeting and ally buffs need explicit contracts.
Independent actor lifetime, attack ownership and deployment clocks are unsupported.

records.sourceDescription: Deploys larger traps that can capture eligible MOAB-class targets.
records.qualification: Persistent traps, capture eligibility, capacity and collection payout require new operations.

records.sourceDescription: Consumes nearby Banana Farms and converts them into Village income; purchase price depends on the Farms absorbed.
records.qualification: Conditional price and consumed actor state cannot become a fixed numeric upgrade cost.

intendedUse.classificationUnit: An explicitly selected build with its base behavior and all purchased effects, not a permanent tower-family role.
intendedUse.resultPolicy: Keep the suggested primary role and its distribution as review data. Never enforce a role from confidence alone.
intendedUse.integration: Optional offline reference catalogue; no TypeSafe dependency in the generator core.
intendedUse.operatorNames: candidateDslOperations are documentation shorthand, not serialized DSL changes.
